claims.text: The driver never entered the pickup geofence. His own trace places all 37 of his fixes 559.37 m from the pickup pin — the minimum, mean and maximum distance are identical at 559.37 m — against an arrival radius of 50 m for this STANDARD zone class. Not one fix qualifies, so there are zero qualifying in-radius fixes, POL-NS-02 is not satisfied and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. The conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 therefore fails at limb (b) and the cancellation fee is not chargeable.

The 'arrived' tap is a false arrival marker. At the recorded arrival event (2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00) the trace puts the driver 559 m from the pin, far beyond the 300 m limit in POL-NS-05, so the marker starts no waiting clock. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip (qualifying_fix_count = 0), limb (ii) of POL-NS-05 applies squarely: the cancellation fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is to be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

On the corrected footing the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds — the longest qualifying run and the accumulated dwell are both 0.00 s — against the 300 second minimum for a STANDARD pickup, a shortfall of 300 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, and that result holds whether or not the rider was present at the pin and whether or not the rider answered any message; the waiting period is the consideration the fee was meant to buy.

The driver's bare assertion that he 'marked arrival and waited' cannot be rescued by the wrong-entrance branch. POL-NS-03 requires the stationary driver to be at a point outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; at 559 m the driver is beyond that 400 m ceiling, so this is not a wrong-face-of-the-same-venue case at all and POL-NS-03 does not engage on either its refund or its compensation side.

The one artifact that could have extended the waiting clock is not on file. EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — and POL-NS-06 limb (i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. The limb is therefore unavailable and there is nothing in the record to convert the driver's 559 m stand-off into in-geofence dwell, so the POL-NS-06 shortfall stands unreduced.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (b) has already failed on the driver's own trace. The anti-farming test is not even reached on these figures — no_show_terminations_30d is 1 and completed_trips_30d is 120, so neither the count nor the rate limb trips — and with no compensation there is no driver-side payment to fund out of this rider's fee.

The driver does not contend that his trace satisfies the arrival geofence: his minimum recorded distance from the pickup pin across the entire window is 559.37 m against an arrival radius of 50 m for this STANDARD zone class, so the POL-NS-01(b) proximity limb is not made out on the GPS and the driver does not assert it. The driver's case rests on the record limbs and on the rider's own conduct, below.

The trip record satisfies the two limbs of POL-NS-01 that turn on the record rather than the trace: it carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-04T07:25:20 (limb (a)), and it shows the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises — with no boarding event recorded, and the termination at 07:31:00 falling after the 5.7 minutes the record books as wait_time_min.

The driver did not abandon the pickup: his trace runs the full window from 07:25:00 to 07:31:00, carries 37 fixes, records 0.0 km travelled and a single distinct speed reading of 0.0 km/h, so he held his position stationary throughout the recorded wait rather than driving off or taking another job while the rider was left waiting.

The rider sent no message at all during the waiting window: the chat log holds only the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 07:25:21 and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40, with no rider message between them. Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 requires at least one locating or coordinating message from the rider, so that rider-exonerating route does not open on this record.

The rider's own device was 519.46 m from the pickup pin at every recorded fix across the window — far outside the 100 m rider_presence_radius_m this STANDARD zone class sets — and the trace records 0 rider qualifying fixes. On the policy's own presence test the rider did not satisfy limb (c) of POL-NS-04, so the rider's account of waiting at the block is not borne out by the rider's own trace.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard does not bite on this driver: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 gives 0.008, far below the 0.08 rate test. There is therefore no pattern of no-show fee-farming on this driver's record, and this termination is not the product of the exploit that clause guards against.

The fare breakdown is internally sound: the cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.00, equal to the fee_schedule resolution rule's result for this trip — the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) — so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises to set the itemised charge aside on arithmetic grounds.

The fee can stand only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold, and condition (b) fails. The driver's own GPS trace, EV-GPS-09104, places him 559.37 m from the pickup pin at every one of his 37 fixes (min, mean and max are all 559.37 m), against the 50 m arrival radius for this STANDARD pickup. Not one fix falls inside the geofence, so there are zero qualifying in-radius fixes. Condition (c) fails too: the in-geofence dwell is 0 s against the 300 s minimum. POL-NS-02 therefore finds the driver never arrived and gives the rider a full refund of the cancellation fee.

POL-NS-05 puts the same conclusion beyond doubt on the false-arrival route. The driver's 'arrived' tap at 07:25:20 sits at a point 559 m from the pin, far beyond the 300 m limit, so the marker is FALSE and starts no waiting clock. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies: the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver (see referrals). POL-NS-06 agrees: on the corrected footing the effective dwell is 0 s, a 300 s shortfall, and the full refund holds whether or not the rider was present or answered messages.

POL-NS-03 does not engage. Its wrong-entrance branch requires the stationary driver to be within 400 m of the pin; at 559 m he is beyond that ceiling, so there is no pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 and no driver-side refund side to this case.

On the driver's claims: I accept that the trip record carries an 'arrived' event (POL-NS-01(a)) and a RIDER_NO_SHOW termination by the driver (limb (d)), but POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and fails at limbs (b) and (c). I accept that the trace shows the driver stationary at 0.0 km/h across the window — but that records him holding position 559 m from the pickup point, which satisfies no locating test and does not make the fee chargeable. His POL-NS-04 argument is correct and immaterial: the chat log (EV-CHAT-09104) holds only the system 'Your driver has arrived' message and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.', with no locating message from the rider, so POL-NS-04 limb (a) is not met and that clause never opens; the rider's own device also sat 519.46 m from the pin (0 qualifying fixes, outside the 100 m radius), so limb (c) is not met either. The driver's POL-NS-07 anti-farming point is correct (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below 4, and 1/120 = 0.008, below the 0.08 rate test), but compensation is not reached at all because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full; driver_compensation_sgd is therefore null, not the SGD 3.20 the fare model computes. The fare breakdown is sound: the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises.

On the rider's claims: I accept the geofence, false-arrival, dwell and POL-NS-03 analysis above. Her own trace places her 519.46 m from the pin (0 qualifying fixes), but rider presence is not a condition of the refund under POL-NS-05(ii) or POL-NS-06, so it changes nothing. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no separate in-geofence intervals can be summed; that limb could not have extended the clock.

Evidence integrity (POL-NS-08): no artifact is impaired on limbs (a) to (d) — no clock skew (the 07:25:20 arrival matches a GPS fix), no trace gap (37 fixes, 0 s max gap, rider track present), no chat defect (2 messages equals trip_record.chat_message_count), no fare defect. POL-GEN-02 confidence is therefore capped at the weight of the trace that carries the deciding fact, EV-GPS-09104 at 1.0; the driver's statement that he 'marked arrival and waited' is not itself a carrier and does not rescue the fee. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is 0.95, the tap-versus-position conflict is resolved by POL-NS-05, there is no counterparty dispute history, no anti-farming trip (1 < 4), and the deciding fact rests on an unimpaired artifact. The fee is therefore refunded, not held.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: all four conditions must hold, and limb (b) — GPS placement inside the geofence at or before the 'arrived' event — fails decisively. The 'arrived' tap at 07:25:20 therefore also fails under POL-NS-05: at that moment the driver was 559 m away, beyond the 300 m limit, so the marker is FALSE and starts no waiting clock. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) governs — the fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable. The same result follows from POL-NS-06: effective dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, and that clause refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responsive.

To the driver: I accept that you did not abandon the pickup. Your trace runs the full window, records a single speed reading of 0.0 km/h with 0.0 km travelled, the trip record carries the RIDER_NO_SHOW code, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard does not bite on you (no_show_terminations_30d = 1, below the count of 4, and 1/120 = 0.008, far below the 0.08 rate test). But POL-NS-01 requires GPS presence inside the geofence as well as a valid reason code, and at 559 m you were never at the pickup. For the same reason POL-NS-03 does not assist you: its wrong-entrance branch reaches only a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin, and 559 m is outside that ceiling, so neither its refund nor its goodwill side engages. No compensation is payable under POL-NS-07 because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full — the 80 percent figure would have been SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00 fee, but it is not earned here.

To the rider: you win the refund, but be clear about the record. Your own device reads 519.46 m from the pin across the window, outside the 100 m rider_presence_radius_m, and the chat log holds no locating message from you, so POL-NS-04 does not open and you do not need it — POL-NS-06 refunds the fee regardless of rider presence.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09104-01, weight 0.0, no payload) cannot help the driver either: POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed, and there are no in-geofence intervals here to sum in any event.

The evidence I relied on is not impaired under POL-NS-08: the trace has no sampling gap (max_gap_sec 0.0) and well over six fixes across the window, the arrival timestamp coincides with a trace fix so there is no clock skew, the rider_track is present, the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line equals the fee_schedule resolution rule (the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee), so no fare defect arises.

Because the false marker fired and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists, POL-NS-05(ii) directs that this trip be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver; that instruction is carried in the referrals list.
